extracted.intended_audience: state regulators, EPA regional staff, electric utilities/owners of affected EGUs, grid operators (RTOs/ISOs), reliability coordinators, and other stakeholders implementing EPA §111 state plans
extracted.subtask_short: EPA EGU reliability mechanisms in state plans
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and approvable methodologies for including short-term and assurance reliability mechanisms, compliance flexibilities, and documentation/approval processes in state plans implementing EPA standards for affected electric generating units (EGUs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable and Usable Lead-Out Framework (RULOF) use for reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: States may use the RULOF provisions to address circumstances in which reliability or resource adequacy is a concern; where reliability considerations for a particular EGU are fundamentally different from those considered when developing these emission guidelines, the state may particularize compliance obligations (typically by different compliance timelines). RULOF is relevant at the stage of establishing standards of performance and compliance schedules as a state plan is developed or revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments under RULOF will take the form of different compliance timelines. Any delay requiring more than a 1-year compliance date extension must be addressed through a state plan revision using RULOF as the basis. See section X.C.2 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary emissions averaging, trading, and unit-specific mass-based compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: States may allow emission averaging or trading, as well as unit-specific mass-based compliance, as voluntary flexibilities to provide reliability-related benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These flexibilities are optional; states that adopt them must demonstrate their programs achieve an equivalent level of emission reduction compared to unit-specific application of rate-based standards and must apply requirements relevant to the particular flexibility (see section X.D). States may choose whether to allow these flexibilities in their state plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year compliance date extension for control-technology installation delays
rubrics_metrics.description: States may incorporate into their state plans a mechanism allowing compliance date extensions up to 1 year for an existing affected EGU that is in the process of installing control technology and encounters a delay outside the owner/operator's control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible causes include delays in obtaining a final construction permit after a timely and complete application or documented supply chain issues (e.g., transformer backlog). The extension is a flexibility to account for unforeseen and uncontrollable lags, not expressly offered for reliability purposes. The source must demonstrate efforts to comply by required timeframes, that problems were entirely outside its control, and that the source's actions or inactions did not contribute to the delay. The owner/operator must follow state plan procedures for documenting the basis for the extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel one-year extension authority for certain new sources
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may provide a similar 1-year compliance date extension for certain new sources (including new combustion turbines) where delays outside the owner/operator's control prevent meeting compliance obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described in section VIII.N. The same documentation and causation standards apply (delays entirely outside owner/operator control, documented efforts to comply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term reliability mechanism (eligibility and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short-term reliability mechanism is available for states to include in state plans (and included for new sources in NSPS) to provide affected sources additional flexibility during rare, extreme, short-duration emergency events when all available generators are called upon to meet electric demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended as an additional safeguard for EEA-2 and EEA-3 events (NERC EOP-011-2) where the system is under strain. The mechanism is limited to discrete periods tied to declared Energy Emergency Alerts and is meant to enable specific units called upon by reliability entities to increase output or remain online beyond scheduled operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEA level thresholds for short-term mechanism applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The mechanism applies only during an Energy Emergency Alert level 2 (EEA-2) or level 3 (EEA-3) as defined by NERC Reliability Standard EOP-011-2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EEA definitions: EEA-1 indicates all available generation resources in use and concern about sustaining contingency reserves; EEA-2 indicates an energy-deficient Balancing Authority that has implemented operating plans but can still maintain minimum contingency reserves; EEA-3 indicates firm load interruption is imminent or in progress and the BA cannot meet minimum contingency reserves. EPA excludes EEA-1 because it is more preparatory, more discretionary, and less consistently reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility limited to units called upon/instructed to deviate during EEAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Only specific units that were called upon, or otherwise instructed to increase output beyond planned day-ahead or near-term expected output, or asked to remain in operation outside scheduled dispatch during an EEA-2 or EEA-3 event are eligible for the short-term reliability flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility requires proper documentation from the reliability coordinator, balancing authority, or ISO/RTO showing the instruction/request to increase output or remain online. The flexibility is not blanket for all units in an alerted region — only those specifically requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of emission rates during short-term reliability events
rubrics_metrics.description: When a state adopts the short-term reliability mechanism, the calculation of an affected source's emission rate during the alert hours follows specific rules: existing affected sources may apply their baseline emission rate in lieu of their standard of performance for hours corresponding to the alert; new sources may exclude emissions/generation data from the event when determining applicability and may use their Phase 1 performance standard for compliance determinations for those hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These adjustments apply only for the documented hours the unit operated under a revised schedule due to EEA-2 or EEA-3, with required documentation. Annual (or rolling annual for new sources) compliance obligations remain in effect; these are temporary deviations for discrete emergency hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reporting, recordkeeping, and documentation for short-term events
rubrics_metrics.description: States and affected sources must maintain and provide documentation to support use of the short-term reliability mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required documentation includes: (1) documentation that the EEA was in effect from the issuing entity, with exact duration of the event; (2) documentation from the issuing entity that the EEA included the affected source/region where the unit was located; and (3) documentation that the source was instructed to increase output beyond planned day-ahead or near-term expected output and/or was asked to remain in operation outside its scheduled dispatch by a reliability coordinator, balancing authority, or ISO/RTO. This information must be supplied to state regulatory entities and to EPA when demonstrating annual compliance, indicating discrete periods when alternative standards/emission rates were in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan inclusion and public notice requirements for short-term mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of the short-term reliability mechanism in a state plan must be explicit and part of the state's public comment process; the state plan must specify the alternative performance standards for each affected source during events and the parameters of the emergency alerts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans must clearly indicate: the specific parameters of emergency alerts used by the mechanism, the relevant reliability coordinators authorized to issue the alerts in the state, and the compliance entities (i.e., affected sources) covered. Inclusion in the plan affords full notice and opportunity for public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability assurance mechanism for units with cease operation dates (up to 1-year extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: States may include a reliability assurance mechanism in their state plans allowing existing affected sources that have committed to cease operation to obtain up to a 1-year extension of the cease operation date when unforeseen reliability needs require the unit to remain online for a discrete amount of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism is intended for isolated, unforeseen circumstances when the relevant reliability authority determines an EGU scheduled to retire is needed to maintain reliability during the 12 months leading up to or after the scheduled retirement. Extensions are limited to the time substantiated in the application and approved by the appropriate EPA Regional Administrator. The mechanism is not intended for delays in control-technology installation (covered by other compliance flexibilities) or for units subject to obligations to operate for reasons not based on the reliability criteria here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process, approvals, and limitations for reliability assurance extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension requests under the reliability assurance mechanism must be substantiated, approved by the EPA Regional Administrator, and for requests exceeding 6 months must also be submitted to FERC (EPA will seek FERC's advice). Any relief beyond 12 months requires a state plan revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date from which an extension can be given is the enforceable date in the state plan (including cease operation dates prior to Jan 1, 2032). For extension requests greater than 6 months, applications must be submitted to FERC as well as to the appropriate EPA Regional Administrator so EPA can seek FERC's advice. Extensions >12 months require a state plan revision under section X.E.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for reliability Planning Authority certification for assurance claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for relief under the reliability assurance mechanism must include certification from the unit's relevant reliability Planning Authority(ies) that the reliability claims are accurate and that the identified reliability problem exists and requires the specific relief requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is required to ensure that reliability claims are sufficiently well documented. EPA will rely on such certifications (and FERC advice for longer extensions) in adjudicating extension requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual compliance period and allowance for temporary emergency deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: The final emission guidelines require compliance with standards on an annual basis (or rolling annual average for new sources), which provides flexibility for temporary changes in emission performance due to grid emergency conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because compliance is measured annually, temporary deviations during rare emergency hours (documented EEA-2/EEA-3 events) can be accommodated via the short-term mechanism without jeopardizing overall compliance, provided proper documentation and state-plan provisions are followed.
